title: Routing latency skew and expert synchronization drift
summary: Investigation notes for a recurring class of tail-latency spikes observed on MoE-enabled endpoints serving long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants. Root cause appears to be intermittent expert synchronization drift combined with routing-induced memory pressure and prefetch misalignment. Contains repro steps, perf traces, hypotheses tested, and action items.
content:
Background:

Over the past 6 weeks we've seen intermittent p95/p99 tail latency regressions (10-40% increases) on several MoE-enabled model endpoints when serving long-context workloads (>8k tokens). Affected model variants: Llama-70B-moex, Mistral-22B-moex, Qwen-34B-moex (custom sharded expert topology). Issues are most visible under mixed-batch loads with skewed input length distributions (many short + few very long).

Symptoms observed (prod + bench):
- Periodic latency spikes concentrated at expert fan-in/fan-out phases (near routing + gather/scatter ops).
- Flamegraphs show widened kernel gaps between forward attention and expert kernels (~3-15 ms gaps).
- GPU timelines indicate bursts of cudaMemcpy (host<>device) and idle time on some devices while others run expensive expert kernels.
- NVLink/NCCL counters occasionally show elevated cross-device traffic correlating with spikes.
- KV-cache eviction pressure increases in long-context batches when routing fanout causes activation growth.

Repro recipe (local cluster):
1) Start a 4-GPU shard with the same expert placement topology used in prod (2 experts per GPU, top-2 gating).
2) Use the long-context stress harness (bench/long_context_skew.py) with mixed batch: 80% seq=64, 15% seq=2048, 5% seq=8192. Target RPS that causes ~65% GPU utilization in steady state.
3) Attach perf traces: nsight-systems capture, pprof of runtime threads, and our internal token-trace logger (token-trace-service:port).
4) Observe for 10 minutes; reproduce span where p99 jumps by >20%.

Key traces & artifacts (high-level):
- nsys trace id: nsys-2024-11-18-01 (linked in GH PR). Shows device3 idle periods of ~8–12ms while device0/1 run expert kernels.
- pprof export: flame-expert-fanout.svg (spike aligns to gating compute finishing early, but prefetch stage not kicked for some experts).
- perf counters: increased L2 evictions and DRAM traffic during spikes (indicative of activation spill).

Hypotheses considered and tests run:

H1 — Gating variability causes misaligned prefetch scheduling:
- Theory: top-k gating output distribution is uneven per-sample; scheduler assumes deterministic timeline for expert kernels and issues prefetches accordingly. When gating outputs skew (many tokens mapped to a small number of experts), some GPUs finish routing early while others get overloaded; prefetch/kv-warmup for the overloaded devices starts late and causes stalls.
- Test: instrumented gating to emit per-batch expert-load histogram; added dynamic prefetch that starts prefetch as soon as gating for a sample is computed (instead of waiting for batch end).
- Result: dynamic prefetch reduced average stall gap by 40% in bench, p99 latency improved ~12% for Llama variant. No correctness regressions seen.

H2 — Cross-device serialization due to NCCL/alltoall blocking behavior:
- Theory: our all-to-all implementation serializes large fanout payloads when some devices have disproportionate tokens, causing waiting on slower devices and amplifying skew.
- Test: replaced alltoall with split+parallel-send implementation in branch perf/split-alltoall and measured overlap. Also toggled NCCL async API where supported.
- Result: split+parallel reduced tail latency variance but increased peak memory pressure (more outstanding buffers). Best combined with a memory reservation cap.

H3 — KV cache eviction and activation spill increasing memcpy bursts:
- Theory: long-context + routing fanout causes activation sets to grow beyond the per-GPU kv-cache budget, triggering on-the-fly evictions and expensive host-device memcpy to maintain consistency.
- Test: simulated higher kv-cache budget and introduced aggressive prefix caching heuristics. Captured DRAM/L2 metrics.
- Result: With 1.5x kv-cache budget, memcpy bursts reduced and p99 improved slightly, but cost and memory scalability are concerns for large clusters.

H4 — Scheduler backpressure due to mixed-batch fragmentation:
- Theory: fragmentation of large and small sequences in a batch forces repeated kernel launches and idle periods when the scheduler serializes fragments to maintain memory headroom.
- Test: implemented batch-fragment-aware scheduler (frag-aware) that groups fragments by seq-length before routing/gather steps.
- Result: reduced kernel count per token and smoothed device timelines; p95 improved notably but p99 still affected by extreme expert hotness.

Model-specific notes:
- Llama-70B-moex: very sensitive to per-expert hotness. Gating distributions are heavy-tailed for certain instruction-style prompts; dynamic prefetch + frag-aware scheduler gave biggest wins.
- Mistral-22B-moex: narrower FFN dims mean expert kernels are faster but more memory-bound; here DRAM traffic and L2 evictions were dominant signals — increasing prefetch overlap beneficial.
- Qwen-34B-moex: observed more NCCL traffic due to sharding choices; split-alltoall combined with async NCCL gave best results, but requires careful buffer management.

Outstanding observations (weird/unexpected):
- On one cluster (rack-5b) p99 spikes correlated with small packet loss events on the management NIC; degraded RDMA retransmissions seemed to amplify NCCL stalls. We don't have a causal proof but network noise appears to exacerbate skew.
- A couple of traces showed device-level micro-pauses when CUDA context switching happened on nodes that also ran system monitoring daemons — suggests contention between our runtime threads and system cron jobs on memory bandwidth.

Actionable mitigations implemented (short-term):
1) Enable dynamic prefetch by default for MoE endpoints behind a feature flag. Rollout in controlled canary (10% traffic) this week. (PR: perf/dynamic-prefetch #1472)
2) Switch to split+parallel-alltoall in the runtime when expert-load variance exceeds threshold; fallback to NCCL path otherwise.
3) Introduce per-GPU outstanding-buffer cap to prevent OOM from split-alltoall path.

Medium-term changes (next quarter):
1) Improve gating calibration: add a light-weight gating post-process to limit extreme hotness (soft-rebalance) and bias tokens to backup experts when hotness threshold reached. This reduces single-expert overload at minor model-quality risk.
2) KV-cache pressure monitoring & autoscale heuristics: expose per-shard kv-pressure metrics and autoscale policy to temporarily increase cache budget when long-context batches appear.
3) Revisit expert placement & topology: implement a placement optimizer that co-locates complementary experts to reduce cross-device traffic for common routing patterns.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Quantify model-quality impact of gating soft-rebalance (need AB test with held-out eval prompts).
- Should we prioritize adding RDMA health checks into our runtime to detect and route away from noisy NICs? (ENG-4189)
- Memory-cost tradeoffs: what's the ops budget for increasing kv-cache baseline vs. complexity of split-alltoall? Run cost model.
- Investigate deeper why some CUDA context switches show extended pause; instrument host-side processes and kernel scheduling.

Notes to reviewers:
- Traces and raw captures are large — see linked GH PR and Confluence page for nsys exports.
- The pragmatic combo that reduced outages in the canary was dynamic-prefetch + split-alltoall guarded by buffer caps. This is good enough short-term but we should not rely on that forever — mainline plan is gating soft-rebalance + better placement.

Appendix (short checklist):
- [x] Repro harness added (bench/long_context_skew.py)
- [x] Dynamic prefetch impl in runtime (feature flag: moe.dynamic_prefetch)
- [x] Split-alltoall prototype merged behind flag
- [ ] Gating soft-rebalance RFC (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Cost model for kv-cache increase (owner: Liangs)
- [ ] RDMA health probe spike experiment (owner: Chloe)

References:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1472
- Eng ticket: ENG-4127, ENG-4189
- Confluence: moe-routing-deep-dive-2024

End of doc.
